papers.title_in_file: Quantum computing - Quantum Computing Inc (Resource library)
papers.version_note: A web page of publication abstracts, not a paper; one text block with no page breaks.
papers.what_it_is: A Quantum Computing Inc resource-library page listing abstracts, links and patents on entropy computing, quantum Zeno optics and optical Ising machines.

assertions.value: The authors introduce a computing paradigm named entropy computing, which works by conditioning a quantum reservoir to enable the stabilization of a ground state.
quotes: Here, we introduce a novel computing paradigm, entropy computing, that works by conditioning a quantum reservoir thereby enabling the stabilization of a ground state.

assertions.value: The authors state that modern quantum technologies using matter are designed as closed quantum systems to isolate them from the environment, and that this design paradigm greatly constrains scalability and limits practical implementation.
quotes: Modern quantum technologies using matter are designed as closed quantum systems to isolate them from interactions with the environment.
This design paradigm greatly constrains the scalability and limits practical implementation of such systems.

assertions.value: The authors state that they experimentally demonstrate the feasibility of entropy computing by building a hybrid photonic-electronic computer that uses measurement-based feedback to solve non-convex optimization problems.
quotes: we experimentally demonstrate the feasibility of entropy computing by building a hybrid photonic-electronic computer that uses measurement-based feedback to solve non-convex optimization problems.

assertions.value: The authors state that the system uses temporal photonic modes to create qudits, encoding probability amplitudes in the time-frequency degree of freedom of a photon.
quotes: The system functions by using temporal photonic modes to create qudits in order to encode probability amplitudes in the time-frequency degree of freedom of a photon.

assertions.value: The authors state that, with electronic interconnects, an arbitrary Hamiltonian can be encoded and non-convex continuous variables and combinatorial optimization problems solved, and that the paradigm can act as a scalable and versatile platform for a large range of NP-hard optimization problems.
quotes: allows us to encode an arbitrary Hamiltonian into the system and solve non-convex continuous variables and combinatorial optimization problems.
We show that the proposed entropy computing paradigm can act as a scalable and versatile platform for tackling a large range of NP-hard optimization problems.
assertions.reader_inference: The page gives the abstract only; no result or scaling data is on the page.

assertions.value: The page links the entropy computing paper to arXiv 2407.04512 and lists Lac Nguyen as first of its authors.
assertions.anchor: Entropy Computing entry, link and author line
quotes: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.04512 Lac Nguyen, Mohammad-Ali Miri
assertions.certainty_reason: The page states the link and author line itself.

assertions.value: The authors state that interaction-free and measurement-free quantum logic gates can be realized asymptotically on demand for single-atom and single-photon qubits, with the interaction-free feature suppressing decoherence from atomic spontaneous decay.
quotes: we show that asymptotically on-demand interaction-and measurement-free quantum logic gates can be realized for both single-atom and single-photon qubits.
The interaction-free feature suppresses the possibility of qubit decoherence via atomic spontaneous decay

assertions.value: The authors state that the efficiency of their Zeno gates is limited primarily by imprecise control of atom-photon scattering and the finite number of feedback cycles (the page text is cut after the word feedback).
quotes: The efficiency of our Zeno gates is limited primarily by the imprecise control of atom-photon scattering and the finite number of feedback

assertions.value: The authors report an experimental all-optical interaction-free switch using the quantum Zeno effect with a contrast of 35∶ 1 (as printed), and state that the data match a zero-parameter theoretical model.
quotes: achieving a high contrast of 35∶ 1.
The experimental data match a zero-parameter theoretical model for several different regimes of operation

assertions.value: The authors report all-optical modulation with a contrast of 80% via quantum Zeno blockade in a lithium niobate whispering-gallery-mode resonator at a pump peak power of 100μW.
assertions.anchor: Observation of Quantum Zeno Blockade in χ(2) Microresonators, CLEO 2013
quotes: We report observing all-optical modulation with a contrast of 80% via quantum Zeno blockade in a Lithium Niobate whispering-gallery-mode resonator at a pump peak power of 100μW.

assertions.value: The authors state, for two interaction-free Fredkin gates in lithium-niobate microdisks, that the threshold pump peak power for a gate contrast above 100 and a signal loss below 10% is hundreds of microwatts for practical device parameters.
assertions.anchor: Interaction-Free Quantum Optical Fredkin Gates in Microdisks entry
quotes: For both gates, the threshold pump peak power to achieve a gate contrast >;100 and a signal loss <;10% is hundreds of microwatts for practical parameters of the devices.
assertions.reader_inference: The page text prints the inequality signs as >; and <;.

assertions.value: The authors state that with a lithium-niobate microresonator a deterministic phase gate can be realized between single photons with near-unity fidelity.
assertions.anchor: Photonic nonlinearities via quantum zeno blockade entry (PRL 110, 223901 link)
quotes: Considering specifically a lithium-niobate microresonator, we find that a deterministic phase gate can be realized between single photons with near-unity fidelity.

assertions.value: The authors state that a nonlinear optics approach can emulate Ising machines with up to a million spins in the absence of optical imperfections, with tailored all-to-all two-body and four-body interactions.
assertions.anchor: Large-scale Ising emulation entry (Commun. Phys. link)
quotes: we propose and demonstrate a nonlinear optics approach to emulate Ising machines containing many spins (up to a million in the absence of optical imperfections) and with tailored all-to-all two and four-body interactions.

assertions.value: The authors report that a nonlinear optical Ising machine shows two distinct ferromagnetic-to-paramagnetic phase transitions, one second-order and one first-order, corroborated by Monte Carlo Metropolis-Hastings simulation.
assertions.anchor: Observation of distinct phase transitions entry
quotes: we experimentally observe two distinct ferromagnetic-to-paramagnetic phase transitions: a second-order phase transition where the magnetization changes to zero continuously and a first-order phase transition
Our experimental results are corroborated by a numerical simulation based on the Monte Carlo Metropolis-Hastings algorithm
